newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet says too soon to talk of At&T taking stake.
newsitem.headline: Stet says too soon to talk of At&T taking stake.

text.p: Officials of Italian telecoms group Stet said it was too soon to talk about AT&T taking part in Stet's privatisation or joing Stet's core shareholding.
They were speaking at a news conference to present the global alliance forged between the two groups on Wednesday.

Stet chairman Guido Rossi, replying to a question about when a decision might may made on a possible share swap between Stet/Telecom Italia and the U.S. group, said any hypothesis "will be evaluated by mid-September."
Asked if Stet was interested in taking a stake in AT&T, Rossi replied, "No, however there is a galaxy of companies in which we are interested."
Stet managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano, referring to a possible share swap, also said it was too soon to speculate about the group's privatisation operation, scheduled for this autumn.
"We will pursue with every good intention whatever future form a further reinforcement of the alliance might take," he added.
John Walter, AT&T Corp president, had also said earlier that it was too early to talk about taking an equity stake in Stet.
